title: The torsion bound over a weakly contractible base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], let $p:X\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ bound the Krull dimensions of all geometric fibres [def-pc-base-change, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $V\to Y$ be an affine weakly contractible object of $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and set $X_V=X\times_YV$, with projection $p_V:X_V\to V$. The scheme $V$ need not be Noetherian. Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ be a locally closed immersion, factor it as $S\xrightarrow{u}\overline S\xrightarrow{i}X$ with $u$ open and $i$ closed, and put $a_!=i_*u_!$ [det-lem-int-tensor-projection]. Write $\mathcal O_{E,T}=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ for the coefficient ring object pulled back from the condensed topological valuation ring [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $L_0$ be a lisse finite free $\mathcal O_{E,S}$-module, meaning a module object [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] which on a pro-étale covering is a finite direct sum of $\mathcal O_{E,S}$. For $n\ge1$ put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$, using its finite discrete constant coefficient sheaf. Then the relative derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] has a natural isomorphism
$$
(a_!L_0)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(A_n)_X\simeq a_!(L_0/\pi_E^nL_0).
$$
Its right-hand side is a sheaf in degree zero and is classical constructible: it is $\nu_X^*F_n$ for a constructible étale $A_n$-module sheaf $F_n$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. If $r:X_V\to X$ is the other projection and $r^*$ is finite constant-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], then pro-étale cohomology [def-sfb-finite-derived-global-sections] satisfies
$$
H^q(X_V,r^*a_!(L_0/\pi_E^nL_0))=0\qquad(q>2d).
$$

proof.text: Put $Q_n=L_0/\pi_E^nL_0$. By [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution], derived reduction is the two-term complex $[L_0\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}L_0]$ in degrees $-1,0$. On a covering trivializing $L_0$, multiplication by $\pi_E^n$ is injective on each of its finitely many coefficient summands, by the same node's exact coefficient sequence. Thus its kernel sheaf is zero, its cokernel is $Q_n$, and $L_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}(A_n)_S\simeq Q_n[0]$. On this covering $Q_n$ is finite free over the finite constant ring $A_n$, so it is locally constant with finite values. Finiteness of $A_n$ is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect].

source.place: Reduction paragraph: flat lattice and finite quotient

proof.text: The field $k$ has only two ideals and its one-point spectrum is quasi-compact. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ a Noetherian scheme. By the affine-cover definition [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compactness choose finitely many affine opens with Noetherian coordinate rings. Each has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. Any ascending chain of opens of $X$ stabilizes on each chart, hence on $X$ by taking the maximum of these finitely many stabilization indices. The closed subspace $\overline S$ is topologically Noetherian as well: if $O_m=\overline S\cap W_m$ is an ascending chain of opens there, replace $W_m$ by $\bigcup_{j\le m}W_j$ to obtain an ascending lifting chain in $X$. By [def-weil-constructible-subset], every subset of these topologically Noetherian spaces is retrocompact. In particular the complementary open of $i$ and the open $S\subseteq\overline S$ are retrocompact; hence their open immersions, including $u$, are quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with $A=\mathcal O_{E,X}$ to $i$. The coefficient isomorphisms $f^{-1}\mathcal O_{E,T}\simeq\mathcal O_{E,T'}$ of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] identify the theorem's inverse-image ring sheaves with the specified coefficients. Thus $i_*$ is exact for the integral coefficient ring; $u_!$ is exact by [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], so $a_!$ is exact as well. Apply the locally closed projection formula [det-lem-int-tensor-projection] with $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, $M=L_0$, and $L=(A_n)_X$. Its displayed isomorphism and step 1 give $(a_!L_0)\otimes^{\mathbf L}(A_n)_X\simeq a_!Q_n$, with the right side in degree zero by exactness. On the cover of step 1, $Q_n\simeq(A_n)_S^{r}$, the finite constant local model with scalar module $A_n^r$; hence it is constructible on the one-stratum partition of $S$ by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-constructible-open-closed-images] first to $u$ and then to $i$, using the finite discrete condensed ring $A_n$, the quasi-compact open $u$ and the quasi-compact open complementary to $i$ just checked. This gives a finite constructible stratification on whose pieces $a_!Q_n$ is locally finitely presented. Over a finite constant ring such a presentation is locally constant with finite values: locally write it as the cokernel of a finite matrix, trivialize the finitely many locally constant entries of that matrix, and take the constant finite cokernel. Thus $a_!Q_n$ is intrinsically constructible, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-sheaf-origin] supplies $F_n$ and $\nu_X^*F_n\simeq a_!Q_n$.

proof.text: The base change $p_V$ is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. To verify its fibre-dimension hypothesis, let $T$ be any finite-type fibre over its residue field $K_0$ and let $K/K_0$ be a field extension. A finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ of $T$ pulls back to the cover $\operatorname{Spec}(B_j\otimes_{K_0}K)$ of $T_K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and the fibre-product identities [def-pc-base-change]. The empty scheme stays empty. If $T$ is nonempty, a nonzero $B_j$ stays nonzero under this scalar extension (a $K_0$-basis becomes a $K$-basis), so $T_K$ is nonempty too. For both nonempty schemes, [lem-pc-dimension-affine-open-cover] and [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] express topological dimension as the supremum of these chart ring dimensions. Each chart dimension is unchanged by [lem-pc-dim-base-change], so $\dim T_K=\dim T$. Applied first to $X_y$ and $\overline{\kappa(y)}/\kappa(y)$, this turns the geometric-fibre bound into the ordinary-fibre bound. For $v\in V$ mapping to $y$, the fibre-product identity identifies $(X_V)_v$ with $X_y\times_{\kappa(y)}\kappa(v)$; another application gives the same bound $d$. Restriction compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies $r^*a_!Q_n$ with $\nu_{X_V}^*F_{n,V}$, where $F_{n,V}$ is the étale inverse image of $F_n$ along $r$. The underlying abelian étale sheaf $F_{n,V}$ is killed by the positive integer $|A_n|$: the finite additive group of $A_n$ is killed by its order, and its unit therefore satisfies $|A_n|\cdot1=0$. Apply [lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound] to $p_V$ and this torsion abelian sheaf to obtain $R^qp_{V,\mathrm{et},*}F_{n,V}=0$ for $q>2d$. The theorem imposes no Noetherian condition on $V$.

By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $p_V$ is separated and of finite type. Finite type includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] makes it quasi-separated. Therefore [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] applies to $p_V$ and the bounded-below étale abelian complex $F_{n,V}[0]$, with discrete coefficients $\mathbf Z$. It gives $Rp_{V,\mathrm{proét},*}\nu_{X_V}^*F_{n,V}\simeq\nu_V^*Rp_{V,\mathrm{et},*}F_{n,V}$. Since comparison inverse image is exact, taking cohomology shows $R^qp_{V,\mathrm{proét},*}(r^*a_!Q_n)=0$ for $q>2d$. Work here with the underlying abelian sheaves throughout; no change between integral condensed and constant coefficient categories occurs in this comparison.

The hypothesis on $V$ is categorical weak contractibility [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]. It also holds for the terminal object of $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Indeed [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies that site with $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}/V$, and [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable] identifies its set sheaves with $\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proét}})/h_V$. An epimorphism $e:F\to G$ in this latter slice is an epimorphism of underlying sheaves: given maps $b,c:G\to T$ with $be=ce$, pair them with the structure map $G\to h_V$ to obtain maps $G\to T\times h_V$ over $h_V$; the slice epimorphism gives their equality and hence $b=c$. For a section $t:h_V\to G$ over $h_V$, projectivity of $h_V$ now gives a lift $s:h_V\to F$ with $es=t$. Since $e$ is over $h_V$, the composite of $s$ with $F\to h_V$ is the identity. The fibre formula of the equivalence identifies $t$ and $s$ precisely with sections over the terminal object of the localized site. Thus evaluation at that terminal object sends every set-sheaf epimorphism to a surjection. With the constant ring $\mathbf Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-weakly-contractible-evaluation-exact] therefore makes $\Gamma(V,-)$ exact on abelian sheaves on $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$. No implication from categorical contractibility to a ring-theoretic criterion is used.

proof.text: Put $G=r^*a_!Q_n$. By [def-sfb-finite-derived-global-sections], $R\Gamma$ is the right derived functor of sections. Derived direct-image composition [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], applied with constant ring $\mathbf Z$ and the global-section morphism to the point, gives $R\Gamma(X_V,G)\simeq R\Gamma(V,Rp_{V,*}G)$. Since $\Gamma(V,-)$ is exact by the preceding step, the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] computes the right-hand side by applying $\Gamma(V,-)$ termwise to any representative $C^\bullet$ of $Rp_{V,*}G$. Exactness preserves the kernels, images and quotients defining $H^q(C^\bullet)$, so $H^q(X_V,G)\simeq\Gamma(V,H^q(C^\bullet))=\Gamma(V,R^qp_{V,*}G)$. Step 4 makes this zero for $q>2d$.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the isolated imported statement omitted the standing finite-type setting needed for constructibility and retrocompact-complement exactness. Restored that setting explicitly, made condensed integral and finite constant coefficient rings and restriction to X_V explicit, and expanded the original four paragraphs into six steps using existing nodes only. See report.md for the non-quasi-compact-open counterexample and source audit. Replaced the ring-theoretic exact-sections citation by the general categorical evaluation theorem, proving passage to the localized site explicitly; used the exact-derived-functor statement to avoid an uncited injective-resolution existence assertion. Second reading makes the scheme-to-topological Noetherian implication explicit, checks exactness over the integral ring using arbitrary-ring open/closed recollement and the coefficient isomorphism, and supplies the affine-cover and topological-dimension statements needed to pass the ring dimension theorem to scheme fibres.
